main_body: A hexagonal wooden coffin with a gold cross on its lid, drawn as a flat lid seen from above, with only a thin dark base strip below
top_band: none distinct: the column runs rows 2-6 mid brown, then a cross bar at row 7, then a long uniform brown lid run to rows 23-24; no lighter top band separated from a front face
evidence: The whole coffin is one tall lid slab with a cross on it, like the red 'top-down slab' in the guide. At x=10 rows 8-23 are a single run of L=109, and rows 25-29 form a darker block (L=70) that is only a base patch at the foot, not a front face under a top. There is no top band, no front-edge line and no eave shadow, so no horizontal top and front face pair can be read. A thin 1px orange line at row 24 does not make a front edge. The result is a top-down plan with the front face missing.

style.evidence: The outline is a tinted dark brown (0% neutral dark edge pixels), which matches Beodeul practice. The coffin has about 4 brown/orange steps plus a gold cross, so shading is thinner than the 5-6 in the references. It has 10 distinct colours and a median of 8 per tile, against 38-40 colours and 17-20 per tile in the references, which is much less detailed overall. Flat-fill coverage is 0%, but the lid areas are smooth with little grain or texture dots. Next to the stall and well it looks simpler and flatter, so it fails.
